thread:
alex: quick heads-up — started a TF + Pulumi wiring prototype for onboarding the new 'sea3' GPU region. goal: reusable modules + clear state/ci handoff. posting notes and a short checklist for review.

sophia: nice. are we going to use S3 + Dynamo for terraform state locking or try GCS backend this time?

alex: S3 + Dynamo for now — aligns with existing infra and cross-account access. pulumi state will also sit in s3 (same bucket, different prefix) with KMS encryption. open to pushback.

chris: +1 for consistency. just make sure the dynamodb table has proper TTL disabled (we ran into auto-ttl issues last quarter). also add a tag policy so costs show up by region.

lina: can you paste the backend snippets? helps me run a quick smoke.

alex: sure — core snippets below. these are intentionally minimal; we'll templatize in the module.

```terraform
terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket         = "redwood-terraform-state"
    key            = "regions/sea3/infra.tfstate"
    region         = "us-east-1"
    dynamodb_table = "tf-state-locks"
    encrypt        = true
  }
}
```

```bash
# pulumi login and stack bootstrap
pulumi login s3://redwood-pulumi-state/sea3
pulumi stack init prod-sea3
pulumi config set aws:kmsKey arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-1234 --secret
```

alex: short validation checklist I'm planning to run before handoff:
- terraform init against a sandbox account (verify state create + lock)
- pulumi login + stack init (verify encryption + object lifecycle)
- net boundaries: VPC ranges, IGW/NAT, and peering routes validated by routing tests
- IAM: cross-account roles + least-privilege for CI service principal
- quota checks for GPUs + subnet IP capacity in sea3
- cost tagging enforced on all resources
- cicd: pipeline runs (plan/apply separation) with manual approval for prod

sam: for the KMS piece — do we want customer-managed key (CMK) or use account-managed? CMK preferred for Private customers. if CMK, add a step to share key policy with the other accounts.

alex: noted. default to CMK and document the key-sharing step in the runbook.

jason: network question — are we doing shared services VPC in the region or dedicated per-customer? affects route table automation.

alex: we support both, but the module will default to shared-services VPC with flags to create dedicated per-tenant VPCs. will include route table automation and a flag to disable peering.

chris: CI wiring — I recommend using ephemeral IAM creds for the pipeline and storing long-lived secrets only in the vault with rotation. also add an integration test that deploys a tiny node group to validate GPU scheduling.

alex: yep on rotation + ephemeral creds. will add a lightweight k8s job in the pipeline that checks GPU node readiness and a sample inferencing container.

infra-bot: pipeline "region-onboard-sea3-sandbox" completed: PLAN=success, APPLY=skipped (manual approval required) :white_check_mark:

lina: I'll take the handoff for the first canary bring-up. can run through the checklist and pair with alex for the pulumi bits.

alex: thanks — appreciate it. Lina, pairing notes: I'll walk you through: stack init, running plan in sandbox, validating state lock, and running the GPU smoke test. expect ~45m for the pair session.

sophia: one more ask — add a short section in the runbook documenting "rollback triggers" (e.g., failed health checks, quota exhaustion, cost spike > threshold) and explicit rollback commands. saves time during incident.

alex: good call — adding rollback commands and how to revert route peering, revoke peer routes, and destroy stack safely.

chris: also log where the terraform and pulumi state lives in the runbook (exact s3 prefixes), and who has access. least-privilege A/C list helps auditors.

alex: will include. final action items: Lina (owner) — run canary and confirm, Chris — verify tags + IAM policy review, Sam — KMS key policy + share, Sophia — add rollback section to runbook, Alex — templatize backend configs and open PR for module + CI pipeline.

lina: ack. scheduling the canary pair for tomorrow 10:00 AM.

alex: perfect. PR link will follow in this thread once opened. thanks all!
